findings.detail: Py_XDECREF(tuple_args) at line 541 may release the last reference; 'args' is then dereferenced here -- 'args' and 'tuple_args' are aliases (assigned together in one '=' chain). Hoist the read above the release, or hold a reference across it

'seq' was loaded from it->it_seq before PySequence_GetItem ran, which can execute arbitrary Python; a re-entrant call can clear it->it_seq and drop the reference first, so this Py_DECREF(seq) drops it a second time. Use Py_CLEAR(it->it_seq) instead of the it->it_seq = NULL / Py_DECREF(seq) pair

'subclasses' is a borrowed reference from lookup_tp_subclasses() (field tp_subclasses) taken at line 783 with no Py_INCREF; PyList_Append can run arbitrary Python before it is dereferenced here (a later iteration's use follows this iteration's call). Re-entrant code that clears the field drops the last reference and this dereference reads freed memory. No site in this file takes a strong reference on lookup_tp_subclasses()'s result, so confirm the field cannot be cleared re-entrantly before dismissing.
